evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'we might need ten to fifteen minutes of your time to put an estimate for you' but no explicit 'Does that sound good?' wait; customer says 'Yeah, this is a good time' which she takes as consent but the framing lacks the full promise structure.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Jeline asks 'if you have any worries or concerns about your move' but this happens AFTER she's already confirmed the pickup address and property details — probing has begun.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'Nope' to concerns, so no follow-up needed — N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised by customer, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers property type (1-bedroom apartment), floor/stories (two floors, first floor for pickup/dropoff), parking (can park in front), rooms (bedroom), walking distance (longer than 25 steps at dropoff), special considerations (mirror and TV flagged as fragile, one small TV under 60 inches, metal bed frame, dresser, light shelves, 4–5 boxes), and dropoff location. Furniture inventory highly detailed.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asks 'do you think you would fall within that range' (15–25 boxes for 1-bedroom) and customer confirms yes. Later probes specific item counts (mirror, TV, dresser, shelves, bed, boxes).
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives hourly rate ($105/hr per mover, $210 for two), minimum (2.5 hours), and personalization to this move ('only moving a one bedroom worth of items with only few boxes, so minimum of 2.5 hours'). However, no comparison to 'typical range for a home this size' — just a specific estimate at the minimum.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee, overnight fee, and materials not disclosed. However, rep does say 'everything is included gas and truck taxes insurance. All the wraps and pads to protect the items when being moved' and explains minimum, prorated in 15-minute increments. Framing is partial — fee transparency absent, but 'not a guess' commitment present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly to scheduling after quoting $525.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No — the Two Promises section was skipped entirely.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'Do you have any questions before I let you go?' — this is the empty throwaway version, not 'What's still concerning you?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep moves directly into scheduling and confirmation without ever asking 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms date (Sunday), arrival window (11 AM–1 PM), pickup address (1300 Summer Oak Drive, Unit A, Austin 78704), dropoff address (1508 Southport Drive, Unit T-155, Austin 78704), and promises to send confirmation email for review. Missing: phone number confirmation, crew size (mentioned 2 movers earlier but not re-confirmed in booking), no notes left for crew about concerns (mirror, TV, fragile items).

top_strength: Excellent logistics probing—Jeline thoroughly documented the bedroom inventory, fragile items, and specific dimensions (TV size, metal bed frame, shelf counts, parking distances), building a highly accurate estimate foundation.
coaching_note: Section 5 (Two Promises) and Section 7 (explicit ask) were both completely skipped—the rep never delivered On-Time Guarantee or Damage Coverage, and never asked 'Would you like our help?' before moving to booking; add these sections back to every full sales call.
booking_note: Customer confirmed the move for Sunday with arrival window 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM: 'That's perfect! I love sleeping in.' Agent stated 'I'll send you know your confirmation email' with date/time/addresses agreed upon.
